To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the gene encoding the Alzheimer's disease-associated amyloid beta peptide is localized to the mouse trisomy 1 region, and is in linkage with two of the three genes previously mapped to the human trisomy 2l region.

1) the gene encoding the Alzheimer's disease (A beta) peptide has been molecularly localized to human chromosome (HSA) 21, band (q)21; 2) the mouse chromosome (MMU) homolog, Cvap, has been localized to band C3----Ter on MMU 6; and 3) the genes Sod-1 and Ets-2 which map to HSA 21 have also been localized to MMU 6,
the gene for the amyloid peptide is localized in the region of the mouse genome which shows the most homology with the Down syndrome critical region of human chromosome 21.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the genetic basis of neurologic disease.
the study of genes that are involved in the pathogenesis of Down syndrome (DS), a genetic disorder which is caused by an extra copy of human chromosome 21.
the study of the neurobiological and behavioral effects of the genetic abnormality in trisomy 17 (Ts17) and trisomy 19 (Ts19) mouse models of Down syndrome (DS).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the mouse model, there is a gene dosage effect of the amyloid precursor protein (APP) on the development and maintenance of the cerebrovascular system and that the APP gene may have a role in the development of Alzheimer's disease in Down syndrome.
the genetic linkage between human chromosome 1 (HSA 1) and mouse chromosome l (MMU 1) is not complete.

the Ts16 mouse is an excellent model for the study of Down syndrome, that the Ts16 model is also a model for the study and understanding of Alzheimer's disease, that the mouse model of Down syndrome and Alzheimer disease is an excellent model to study the effects of trisomy of chromosome 21, and that the Ts16 mice are excellent models for the study of trisomy and Down syndrome.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have cloned the murine homolog of the gene encoding the beta-amyloid protein (AbetaPP) and have localized it to mouse chromosome 16.

the mouse gene encoding the amyloids, the gene encoding superoxide dismutate, and the protoonocogene, Ets 2, are all located in a region of mouse chromosome 16 which has been shown to have genetic homology to the human chromosome 21.
the mouse model is relevant not just to Down syndrome but to Alzheimer's disease as well.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mouse is an appropriate model system for studies of the genes involved in DS and AD.
the mouse trisomy 10 is an excellent model of the human trisomy 17, which in turn is an excellent model for Down syndrome.
the genetic linkage between the amyloid gene and other genes on human chromosome 21 and mouse chromosome 17 is maintained despite the chromosomal rearrangement that changed the gene order in mouse.
